notes: staged $TMPDIR/bench-scratch-list_walk-6-2-1792329586570292981/bench_list_walk.beam (embedded source, LEN=1000, erlc=/nix/store/khp1dd3fk8476mwg62cinwvk5a17r53s-erlang-29.1.1/lib/erlang/erts-17.1/bin/erlc)

method: paired startup-cancelled marginal — every round runs the N-walk pass then the 0-walk pass back to back, and ns/element = median(paired difference) / (N * LEN) * 1e6, withheld below 3x max(1 ms, 1.4826*MAD) of the paired differences; N is per runtime so both marginals are measurable, and the fixed process startup (incl. the Rust runtime's code-path resolution) cancels inside every pair; the module is BIF-free and builds no term
note: element count is deterministic and contention-immune; the wall-clock rows move with host load

results.description: allocate-and-abandon garbage churn under each runtime (per-op GC cost)
notes: staged $TMPDIR/bench-scratch-gc_bound-6-4-1792329629625213794/bench_gc_bound.beam (embedded source, LEN=256, per-op increment=1, erlc=/nix/store/khp1dd3fk8476mwg62cinwvk5a17r53s-erlang-29.1.1/lib/erlang/erts-17.1/bin/erlc)
case churn: paired median=851.381 ms min=846.947 ms max=854.259 ms noise=±2.384 ms over 10 round(s)
observed stdout: churn=N*1=200000
case churn: N=200000 churns (sys), each allocating and abandoning a 256-element list, a 256-byte binary and a 256-element tuple

method: every round runs the program at N churns and then at 0 churns back to back, and ns/op is the median paired difference (wall@N - wall@0) / N * 1e6 — never two separate means, whose difference absorbs a drifting boot cost instead of cancelling it. N is per runtime so both marginals are measurable, the fixed process startup (incl. the Rust runtime's code-path resolution) cancels inside every pair, and a figure inside the noise band is withheld rather than published

note: the op count is deterministic and contention-immune; the wall-clock rows move with host load. Whether a runtime's collector actually runs during the loop is its own admission policy — this row measures the allocate-and-abandon wall time, and claims no collection count

results.description: a writable-accumulator binary append (16 KiB in, 64 KiB out) on both runtimes (ns/call)
notes: staged $TMPDIR/bench-scratch-binary_append-6-5-1792329640664224987/bench_binary_append.beam (embedded source, INPUT_ARG=8192, 65536 bytes out per call, erlc=/nix/store/khp1dd3fk8476mwg62cinwvk5a17r53s-erlang-29.1.1/lib/erlang/erts-17.1/bin/erlc)
case binary_append: paired median=4503.898 ms min=4371.887 ms max=4582.294 ms noise=±89.451 ms over 10 round(s)
observed stdout: binary_append=N*65536=3276800000
case binary_append: N=50000 calls (sys) of expand/1 over a 16384-byte payload, i.e. 3276800000 bytes appended

method: paired startup-cancelled marginal — every round runs the N-call pass then the 0-call pass back to back, and ns/call = median(paired difference) / N * 1e6, withheld below 3x max(1 ms, 1.4826*MAD) of the paired differences; N is per runtime so both marginals are measurable, and the fixed process startup (incl. the Rust runtime's code-path resolution) cancels inside every pair

note: the call and byte counts are deterministic and contention-immune; the wall-clock rows move with host load. Each expand/1 appends 16 384 four-byte segments into one writable payload (the compiler's writable-accumulator squeeze), so the measured path is the binary append, not a series of copies
